what: The gates the Guardrail 3 calibration harness (`e4.9`, `reco-mkl.1`) holds its own measurement to. ADR-001 §5.4 publishes `G3 <= 0.30` at alpha, `<= 0.15` at 1.0 and `miss_rate <= 0.20`, and says out loud that `e4.3` and `m1` defer to "the threshold agreed in `e0.12`"; those numbers are copied into this file from §5.4 and nowhere else, and the harness refuses to run if the alpha threshold here disagrees with the shipped default `risk.tau` — one number, in the document, and a check that the copy did not drift. `cargo run -p fathom-analyze --features sqlite-bundled,langs-all --example g3_calibration -- --check` re-measures them against the three pinned repositories and fails if any gate came out other than declared. The `langs-all` is not decoration: since `reco-l9bz.7` the score carries a cyclomatic-complexity axis, and a build without the grammars silently leaves that axis out of every denominator on the corpus rather than failing.
how_gates_are_set: Every gate declares `expected`: `pass`, `fail` or `not-measurable`. A gate that surprises us in either direction fails the run, because a claim that quietly starts passing has to be re-read just as hard as one that fails. The `fail` gates are the measurement's findings, not its defects: on three real OSS repositories — three windows of 180 episodes each, 540 episodes, 525 of them mature — the shipped score at §5.4's published default τ flags 51 episodes and 31 of them were cost without value, so the α gate measures 0.608; across everything the corpus flags at either cut, 67 flags of which 43 were cost without value, `G3` 0.642; and 20 of the 24 episodes that were mature and later needed rework still sat below τ, a miss rate of 0.833. Those are the numbers `e0.12`'s thresholds have to survive; they are written here rather than smoothed into a sentence. A gate is never adjusted to fit a measurement: the `min_denominator` floor is what turns an anecdote into `not-measurable` instead of into a comfortable `pass`, and when a gate's `expected` changed it changed because the measurement moved — `miss-rate-denominator-is-big-enough` at the `reco-dyt` re-pin (7 → 24 mature reworked episodes), and `every-flagged-episode-is-labelled` twice, where `reco-6co`'s re-score promoted one episode into the flag population and `reco-0zi`'s re-measure — after `reco-0er` took a guessed `human` out of the score's denominator — promoted five: in both cases the promoted diffs were read and written up before the run was blessed, and the gate came back to `pass`. The bars themselves — 0.30, 0.15, 0.20 — have never moved. `reco-l9bz.7` re-measured with a thirteenth feature axis and a sixth ranking component and moved no bar either: 51 of the 58 episodes the previous run had flagged changed score, nine came into a flag population for the first time, five left one, and four of the nine needed a fresh hand reading before the run could be blessed (§3e). Two of the seven numbers moved in the reviewer's favour and one moved against it, and the one that moved against it is quoted in full under `miss-rate-at-published-tau`.
tau_note: §5.4 tightens the *rate* at 1.0 (0.15), not the threshold: tau stays 40 in both gates, so the two `g3-*` gates are one flag set read against two bars. This number moved from 70 to 40 in `reco-6co` and it moved *here*, in ADR-001 §5.4, in the shipped `risk.tau` default, in `fathom.toml` and in the reference policy in the same commit: §5.4 always said its default was to be "confirmed against three real OSS repositories", and the confirmation is this file's own measurement — nothing in 540 real episodes reached 70, so the τ arm of `F(τ,W)` was inert, while τ 40 was the corpus's own top-decile floor and remains the lowest threshold on the grid whose flags are all labelled (see `tau_sweep` in the blessed report). The deciles have moved twice since — 34 / 42 / 43 after `reco-0er` lifted every score by taking an absent axis out of the denominator, and 33 / 39 / 42 after `reco-l9bz.7` added an axis and re-spread the weights — so what binds τ is the labelling floor, not the deciles. The harness's check against the shipped `risk.tau` is what catches a copy that drifted.
labelling_note: ADR-001 §5.4 names §5.4's four false-positive codes as `expected`, `not-applicable`, `low-stakes` and `false-positive`. The closed list that actually shipped is `e4.6`'s (`fathom_analyze::queue::REASONS`), and the mapping is a collapse, not an invention: §5.4's `expected` is shipped `intentional` ("what looks risky here is what I wanted"); §5.4's `low-stakes` and `false-positive` are shipped under their own names; §5.4's `not-applicable` has no separate shipped code — `false-positive`'s claim ("the finding that raised this does not describe my change") already covers the case, so the two measure together and this file says so instead of hiding the collapse. §5.4's true positive `accepted-with-required-change` is shipped `accepted`: `e4.6`'s ledger has no 'with required change' refinement, so a flag that earned a review that happened is the true positive, and rework of the episode counts as one too per §5.4's own `TP(e)` clause. The five shipped codes that are neither (`not-my-area`, `already-known`, `superseded`, `will-revert`, `other`) are dismissals about the reviewer's attention or the queue's state rather than about the flag: they sit in `G3`'s denominator exactly as §5.4 writes it — the reviewer looked, so the flag cost something — and never in its numerator.

gates.claim: at §5.4's published default τ — 40, confirmed against real history by this corpus in `reco-6co` — the aggregate false-positive rate clears the alpha gate
gates.why: Measured 0.608 (31 false positives on 51 labelled flags) against a bar of 0.30, and the number means something now, which is the difference between this read and `e4.9`'s. At τ 70 the flag arm was inert: 6 episodes in 540 reached it, all six through a high-severity finding and none through τ, because `features-1`'s ceiling on this corpus is 66. τ 40 is §5.4's own "confirmed against three real OSS repositories" — it is the shipped `risk.tau`, and the flag population is 51 episodes (9.4 % of the corpus), every one of them carrying a hand-authored disposition. What τ is no longer is the corpus's top-decile floor: the per-repository cuts are 33 / 39 / 42 and two of them now sit above τ. `reco-l9bz.7`'s complexity axis improved this number from 0.660 without claiming credit for it: six episodes that used to be flagged at τ fell below it — five long-dismissed bot and dependency bumps that the re-spread took under the threshold, and one `accepted` `cli` telemetry change quoted under `miss-rate-at-published-tau` — and four rose into it, among them two `accepted` ty changes and a bot's vendored-typeshed sync that was dismissed again and blamed on the ranking. `aggregate.tau_sweep` is still the evidence and the floor: τ 40 is the lowest threshold on the grid whose flags are all labelled — at τ 35 seven of 68 are not — which is what makes this rate an answer about 51 episodes rather than an answer about 61.

gates.claim: across every episode the corpus flagged — §5.4's published τ plus each repository's own top-decile cut, which is what a reviewer would actually have been shown — no more than 30 % of the labelled flags were cost without value
gates.why: Measured 0.642 on 67 labelled flags: 30 dismissed `low-stakes` (Dependabot, renovate and release-bot bumps, and `update dev dependencies` episodes that re-emit the CI workflow templates and a 1 000-line lockfile — the workflow and dependency axes raised them and no finding justified them), 9 `false-positive` (a test spy charged as untested new logic, `# type: ignore` and `#[expect(deprecated)]` suppressions whose reason is written on the line above them, a `"TODO"` that is the name of a GitHub label, a fuzzer's own report charged as leftover debug output, and mdtest — ty's real test surface — counted as no tests at all), and 4 `intentional` (the `gh repo garden` deletion that took its test file with it, and dropping Python 3.10 and the other end-of-life Pythons). 24 of the 43 false positives were blamed on the ranking rather than on a detector (`aggregate.coverage.blamed_on_score`), unchanged from the previous run and now stated honestly: `reco-l9bz.7`'s `features-2` pass added a thirteenth axis to the same ranking a false-positive blame is charged against, and the count did not move — the axis redistributed which bot maintenance got flagged (see `g3-alpha-at-published-tau`) rather than making the ranking's claims truer. The finding still stands and it is still about where the flags come from: the majority of what is left is human-authored maintenance that re-emits CI from an out-of-tree template, which no path rule can see.

gates.claim: the same population clears the 1.0 gate of 0.15
gates.why: Measured 0.642 on the same 67 labelled flags against the 1.0 bar of 0.15 — the identical number as `g3-alpha-at-corpus-cut`, because §5.4 tightens the rate at 1.0 and leaves τ alone (see `tau_note`). `reco-l9bz.7` moved it from 0.683 and moved it in the right direction; the distance to the bar is still a `fail` and it is still the same finding about where flags come from, so it stays open at `m1`.

gates.claim: at the published default τ, no more than 20 % of the episodes that later needed rework sat below the flag threshold
gates.why: Measured 0.833 (20 of the 24 mature episodes that were later reverted, fixed or follow-up-fixed on the same files never reached τ 40) against a bar of 0.20, and `reco-l9bz.7` made it *worse* by one episode: `cli`'s `start attachment telemetry before asset validation` (`ep-859df55bc1cfcaf5735e`, `accepted`, later reworked) sat at exactly 40 under `features-1` and lands at 37 under `features-2`, because the new axis paid for itself by taking weight off the shape axes it was measured against. That is the whole cost of the change, stated here rather than in a footnote: an axis that separates conceptual complexity from churn earns its weight by moving the middle of the distribution, and the middle is where the rework lives — `features-2`'s maximum on this corpus is 64, so the ceiling moved too and none of it came back as recall. The other 19 misses are the shape this metric was added to catch, and they are ordinary-looking source edits that no threshold set catches by moving τ: at τ 35 the sweep reaches 18 of the 24 (miss 0.750) by flagging 68 episodes — 12.6 % of the corpus, 7 of them unlabelled. The bars did not move, and the rework in these windows did not become more distinguishable.

gates.claim: at each repository's own top-decile cut — the queue a reviewer would actually have read first — no more than 20 % of the reworked episodes were below it
gates.why: Measured 0.750 (18 of the 24 fell below their repository's own top-decile boundary — 8 of `cli`'s 10, 8 of `flask`'s 12, 2 of `ruff`'s 2) against a bar of 0.20. This is the recall read a reviewer would actually get, because a queue is ordered by score and the cut is where the reading stops, and it is the first number in the `tau_sweep` to stop being a τ artefact. `reco-l9bz.7` left every count in it exactly where it was while moving all three cuts — `cli` 34 → 33, `flask` 42 → 39, `ruff` 43 → 42 — which is the most honest possible result for a re-score: the boundary moved under the episodes and the episodes moved with it. The bars never moved, and this one is still open.

gates.claim: the corpus contains at least 20 mature reworked episodes, which is what a 0.20 gate on a rate needs to be able to tell 0.20 from 0.60
gates.why: Measured 24 mature reworked episodes out of 525 mature, which clears the floor of 20: the rate above it is a rate over 24 episodes and is stated as such everywhere it appears. The floor was set by the same pass that set the bar in the first place (`reco-dyt`) and it has been met ever since the windows were widened to 180 episodes.

gates.claim: every episode any cut flagged has a hand-authored disposition — a flag nobody labelled is a hole in the guardrail, and a guardrail with a hole in it is not a guardrail
gates.why: Measured 0 unlabelled episodes across the 67 flags this run raised (76 hand-authored dispositions in the corpus, 9 of them on episodes below every cut). `reco-l9bz.7`'s complexity axis promoted nine episodes into a flag population for the first time and five out of one; four of the nine had never been flagged before and so had never been read, and each is now read and dispositioned against its own diff in `truth.json` — a `cli` telemetry-lifecycle rewrite (`accepted`), a vendored-typeshed sync taken over τ by the axis itself (`dismissed`, `low-stakes`, blamed on the ranking), a ty solver change that tightens which generic solutions may be inferred (`accepted`) and a new `flake8-type-checking` runtime-ambiguity notion with a new setting behind it (`accepted`). The gate is the mechanism by which a re-score is forced to say what it promoted; it went red mid-pass and came back green on the read, which is the only way this file has ever gone green.

gates.claim: the corpus flags at least 20 episodes, below which `G3` is a story about a handful of commits rather than a rate
gates.why: Measured 67 episodes flagged across the union of τ and the three per-repository top-decile cuts, against a floor of 20: 12.4 % of the corpus, which is a queue and not a handful. The population is the gate on every `G3` number on this page, and `reco-l9bz.7`'s axis is what put the fourth percentage point of it there.

gates.claim: no detector is disqualified by `e0.12`'s rule as this harness scores it: a default-enabled detector whose own false-positive rate breaches the alpha gate on at least 8 answerable flags (the bar a default flip has to clear, deliberately higher than the 5 a printed number has to clear) is a detector that must ship disabled. Read `why` before reading the 0 as a clean bill of health.
gates.why: Measured 0 enabled detectors that breached α with 8 or more flags, on the flag population of 67. Read §4 of the calibration page before trusting the sentence: every enabled detector answers 100 % of its flags and the seven zero-severity ones cannot enter this metric at all, so `pass` here means "no enabled detector was measured to be bad", which is not "the detectors are calibrated".
